verdict.rationale: Moss documents its own API key management: keys can be created, listed and deleted from the CLI, rotated with overlap, and a pattern is given for browser or untrusted clients so the projectKey is never shipped in client code. Nothing shows roles or per-index (per-collection) permissions, so the granular part of the story is unevidenced. Missing for 10: role-based access control, per-index/per-collection permission scoping, scoped or read-only keys, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can enforce granular access control (API keys, roles, per-collection permissions) on database operations

citations.quote: You can also manage keys from the terminal with the Moss CLI: `moss login`, then `moss keys create`, `list` or `delete`.
Rotate with overlap. Create a new key, move your clients to it, then delete the old one.
Use this pattern from browser or untrusted clients where the `projectKey` must never be embedded in shipped code.
